learning_outcomes.text: Students master the basics of linear algebra and multi-dimensional analysis. They can confidently handle vectors, matrices, and functions of several variables. They understand central concepts such as vector space, invertibility, and partial differentiability, and are familiar with important statements regarding these. Students can comprehend the justifications for these statements presented in the lecture and independently justify simple statements building upon them. They can easily solve application-relevant problems where derivatives or integrals in multiple dimensions are relevant. In doing so, they are independently able to identify and apply the correct techniques.

Students are able to work in teams and have deepened their knowledge of mathematics as a common language. They can review complex concepts, pinpoint open questions, and seek targeted help if necessary. In doing so, students have developed high perseverance and can work purposefully on difficult problems.

syllabus_topics: Matrices and vectors, vector space, determinants
Scalar product, norms, lengths and angles in Rn
Differential calculus for functions of several variables
Divergence and curl, theorems of Stokes, Green and Gauss

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam (30 minutes, individual exam) if < 10 participants

assessment_rules: Homework exercises are required as a prerequisite for the exam. The exam is a 120-minute written exam if there are 10 or more participants. If there are fewer than 10 participants, the exam will be a 30-minute individual oral exam. Successful completion of practice assignments in homework and/or in-class exercises is required for the award of credit points.
